title: Vendor risk review
description: One review of a third-party relationship: what the third party provides, what data and access it has, how critical the relationship is, inherent and residual risk, the assessments performed, findings and their remediation or acceptance, the review cadence, and the decision and its approvals. The structure follows the third-party risk management life cycle in the US banking agencies' Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management (OCC Bulletin 2023-17), with supply chain concepts from NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 and ISO/IEC 27036. It records a review; it doesn't prescribe how to tier vendors or score risk, and using it does not by itself satisfy any of that guidance.

$schema.title: Schema
$schema.description: The `$id` of the schema the record follows, so a reader can tell what the record is without guessing. Optional; recordType and schemaVersion say the same thing.

recordType.title: Record type
recordType.description: Always vendor-risk-review. Lets a reader (or validate()) tell the format apart from the others in this repository.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The version of this format the record follows. Each version of the schema accepts only its own version string, so a record never silently passes against a schema it wasn't written for.

id.description: This review's identifier, unique within the system that created it. A relationship reviewed every year has one record per review, each with its own id; link them through vendor.id or externalIds.

externalIds.title: External identifiers
externalIds.description: Ids for this review in other systems: the GRC tool, procurement, the contract repository.

updatedAt.description: When the record was last changed.

reviewingOrganization.description: The organization doing the review (the bank, hospital or agency that relies on the third party). Optional because it is usually obvious inside one organization; give it when records are shared or consolidated.

vendor.description: The third party under review. The interagency guidance uses third-party relationship broadly: vendors, service providers, fintech partners, affiliates and others.

relationshipOwner.description: The person inside the organization accountable for the relationship day to day (often the business line manager), as distinct from the risk staff who assess it.

lifecycleStage.title: Lifecycle stage
lifecycleStage.description: Where the relationship is in the third-party risk management life cycle of the interagency guidance (OCC Bulletin 2023-17): planning; due-diligence (the guidance's Due Diligence and Third-Party Selection); contract-negotiation; ongoing-monitoring; or termination. The guidance treats oversight and accountability, independent reviews, and documentation and reporting as running throughout the life cycle rather than as stages, so they are not values here. In September 2026 the agencies proposed replacement guidance (OCC Bulletin 2026-46) organized around risk management components rather than these stages; this field follows the 2023 guidance, which applies until any replacement is final.

services.title: Services
services.description: What the third party provides under the relationship, one entry per distinct service or product. At least one is required, because a review is always of something specific.

items.title: Service
items.description: One service or product the third party provides.

name.title: Name
name.description: The service's name, as the business knows it.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the service does for the organization, in a sentence or two a reviewer outside the business line would understand.

supportsCriticalActivity.title: Supports a critical activity
supportsCriticalActivity.description: Whether the service supports a critical activity as the organization defines it. The interagency guidance (OCC Bulletin 2023-17) describes critical activities as ones that could cause the organization to face significant risk if the third party fails to meet expectations, have significant customer impacts, or have a significant impact on its financial condition or operations, and leaves each organization to identify its own. Higher-risk and critical activities call for more rigorous oversight.

startDate.description: When the service started or will start.

endDate.description: When the service ends or ended (contract expiry or exit). Must not be before startDate.

contractRef.title: Contract reference
contractRef.description: The contract, order or statement of work that covers the service, as the contract repository names it.

annualSpend.description: Expected or actual spend per year, used for tiering and concentration analysis.

dataCategories.title: Data categories
dataCategories.description: The kinds of the organization's data the third party stores, processes or can reach, as many as apply; use none, on its own, when it has no access to the organization's data. Values: none; public; internal; confidential (business confidential); personal-data (information about an identifiable person); sensitive-personal-data (special-category or high-risk personal data such as government ids, financial account numbers, biometrics); nonpublic-personal-information (consumer information protected under the US Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act; not employee data); protected-health-information (as defined by HIPAA); payment-card-data (cardholder data in scope for PCI DSS); controlled-unclassified-information (US federal CUI); authentication-credentials (passwords, keys, tokens that grant access); source-code.

access.title: Access
access.description: How the third party reaches the organization's systems and data, and where the data goes.

systemAccess.title: System access
systemAccess.description: The highest level of access the third party (or its staff) has to the organization's own systems: none; read; read-write; or administrative (can change configuration, users or security settings).

hostsData.title: Hosts data
hostsData.description: Whether the third party stores the organization's data on infrastructure it controls (including its cloud providers), rather than only reaching it inside the organization's systems.

dataLocations.title: Data locations
dataLocations.description: Countries where the third party stores or processes the data, including through subcontractors. Matters for data transfer law, government access and resilience planning.

subcontractors.title: Subcontractors
subcontractors.description: The third party's own suppliers that support the service or touch the data. The interagency guidance calls these subcontractors; many programs call them fourth parties. NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 treats them as part of the supply chain the organization must understand.

service.title: Service
service.description: What the subcontractor does for the third party.

country.description: Where the subcontractor performs the work.

criticality.title: Criticality
criticality.description: How much the organization depends on the relationship, on its own tiering scale mapped to four levels: low, moderate, high or critical. Reserve critical for relationships that support critical activities (see services[].supportsCriticalActivity). Rigor of due diligence, monitoring and contract terms should scale with this rating.

criticalityRationale.title: Criticality rationale
criticalityRationale.description: Why the relationship has that criticality, in terms an examiner can follow: what would happen if the service failed.

inherentRisk.description: Risk before the organization's and the third party's controls are taken into account, based on the service, data, access and criticality.

residualRisk.description: Risk remaining after controls, given what the assessments showed. The gap between inherent and residual risk is what the controls are credited with.

riskDomains.title: Risk by domain
riskDomains.description: Inherent and residual risk for each risk domain assessed. Optional; many programs rate only overall risk.

items.title: Domain rating
items.description: The rating in one risk domain.

residual.description: Residual risk in this domain, once assessed.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: What drives the rating, including the controls that reduce it.

assessments.title: Assessments
assessments.description: The due diligence and monitoring work performed for this review: questionnaires, document and independent report reviews, visits, financial reviews, test reviews. Findings point at the assessment that raised them.

id.description: Identifier for the assessment, unique within the review; findings refer to it.

type.title: Type
type.description: questionnaire (security or due diligence questionnaire); document-review (policies, plans, insurance, contracts); independent-report-review (an independent audit or certification report, for example a SOC 1 or SOC 2 report, an ISO/IEC 27001 certificate or a PCI DSS attestation); onsite-visit; remote-assessment (interviews or walkthroughs by video); financial-review (financial statements and condition); penetration-test-review; continuous-monitoring (outside-in security ratings, news, sanctions or financial alerts); other.

evidenceName.title: Evidence name
evidenceName.description: The report, certificate or questionnaire reviewed, named the way its issuer names it.

periodStart.description: Start of the period the evidence covers (for a SOC 2 Type 2 report, the start of its examination period).

periodEnd.description: End of the period the evidence covers. Must not be before periodStart; a stale period (long before the review) is itself worth a finding.

result.title: Result
result.description: satisfactory; satisfactory-with-findings (acceptable, with findings recorded below); unsatisfactory; or inconclusive (not enough evidence to conclude, for example an unanswered questionnaire).

attachmentIds.description: Ids of the evidence files in the record's attachments.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: Issues found during the review and what is being done about each: remediation, or a documented risk acceptance.

reviewCadence.title: Review cadence
reviewCadence.description: How often the relationship is reviewed and when the next review is due, plus the events that should prompt an earlier review. Cadence normally follows criticality.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.description: monthly, quarterly, semiannual, annual, biennial (every two years) or event-driven (no fixed schedule; reviewed only on a trigger).

lastReviewedOn.description: When the last review was completed.

nextReviewDue.description: When the next scheduled review is due. Must not be before lastReviewedOn.

triggers.title: Event triggers
triggers.description: Events that prompt a review outside the schedule.

items.description: One trigger event, in a few words.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: The outcome of the review, once one is made.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: approved; approved-with-conditions (conditions must be listed); rejected (don't enter or renew the relationship); deferred (more information needed before deciding); or terminate-relationship (exit an existing relationship).

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: Conditions attached to the approval, each specific and checkable. Required, and must not be empty, when the outcome is approved-with-conditions.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why the decision was made, especially when it accepts elevated residual risk.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description: Sign-offs on the decision, in the order they were given. Who must approve depends on the organization's policy and the relationship's criticality (critical relationships often go to a committee or the board).

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.description: The role in which the person approves, which is what policy requires (a person may hold several).

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: approved, rejected or abstained (for example because of a conflict of interest).

comment.title: Comment
comment.description: What the approver said, if anything.

status.description: Where the review is in its workflow: draft; in-review (assessments under way); pending-approval; approved; rejected; or closed (complete with no further action, for example after termination). The validator checks approved and rejected agree with decision.outcome.

statusHistory.title: Status history
statusHistory.description: Every status the review has had, oldest first, ending at the current status (the validator checks both).

status.description: The status the record moved to, one of this format's status values.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Files that belong to the review: independent reports, questionnaires, contracts, financial statements. Many are shared under NDA; set classification accordingly.

auditTrail.title: Audit trail
auditTrail.description: Recorded actions on the review, oldest first.

extensions.description: Local fields this format doesn't define, namespaced as <namespace>:<field>, for example examplebank:costCenter.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status values of this format, defined once so status and statusHistory use the same list. Where the review is in its workflow: draft; in-review (assessments under way); pending-approval; approved; rejected; or closed (complete with no further action, for example after termination). The validator checks approved and rejected agree with decision.outcome.

riskLevel.title: Risk level
riskLevel.description: A four-level risk rating: low, moderate, high or critical. Organizations with three or five levels map onto these and keep their own score in riskRating.score.

riskDomain.title: Risk domain
riskDomain.description: A category of risk: information-security; privacy; operational-resilience (ability to deliver through disruption); business-continuity (recovery plans and their testing); financial (the third party's financial condition); compliance (laws and regulations, including consumer protection); legal (contract and liability); reputational; concentration (reliance on one provider, or many relationships on one subcontractor); strategic; geographic (country and location risk); environmental-social (ESG).

riskRating.title: Risk rating
riskRating.description: An overall risk rating with the method and reasoning behind it, so a later reader can tell how it was reached.

score.title: Score
score.description: A numeric score on the organization's own scale, if its method produces one. Not comparable between organizations; level is.

method.title: Method
method.description: The scoring method or model used, with its version.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why the rating is what it is.

finding.title: Finding
finding.description: An issue found during the review: what it is, how severe, what raised it, and whether it is being fixed or its risk accepted.

id.description: Identifier for the finding, unique within the review, used in conditions and follow-up.

title.title: Title
examples: Quarterly user access reviews not evidenced for Q3

description.title: Description
description.description: What was found and why it matters.

domain.description: The risk domain the finding falls in.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: low, medium, high or critical, on the organization's issue-rating scale.

assessmentId.description: The assessment that raised the finding. The validator checks it exists.

status.title: Status
status.description: open; remediation-planned; in-remediation; remediated (fixed, awaiting or past verification); risk-accepted (not being fixed; riskAcceptance is required); or closed.

remediation.title: Remediation
remediation.description: The plan to fix the issue.

plan.title: Plan
plan.description: What will be done, by whom (the third party or the organization).

owner.description: Who is responsible for seeing it done.

verifiedBy.description: Who confirmed the fix works. Separation between the person fixing and the person verifying is what examiners look for.

riskAcceptance.title: Risk acceptance
riskAcceptance.description: A documented decision to accept the risk instead of fixing it: who accepted it, when, why, and until when. Required when status is risk-accepted, because an undocumented acceptance is indistinguishable from an ignored finding.

acceptedBy.description: Who accepted the risk. Should be someone with authority to accept risk of this severity under the organization's policy.

expiresOn.description: When the acceptance expires and must be revisited. Must not be before acceptedAt. Open-ended acceptances are a common examination finding; give a date.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why the risk is accepted, and any compensating controls.
